arguments.summary: A critical firewall integrity alert was triggered by suspicious activity originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), identified as a high-criticality finance department endpoint. Investigation revealed that the host was compromised via a phishing campaign involving malicious PowerShell execution, leading to a Cobalt Strike beacon (C2 communication to 198.51.100.23 on TCP/443). The attacker performed lateral movement via SMB to a file server (10.0.5.50) and attempted Kerberos TGT requests. Despite detection by IDS and EDR systems, containment actions (firewall block, EPP isolation) were denied due to policy or targeting issues. No evidence of data exfiltration was found during sandbox analysis, but host file modification and unsigned DLL loading were confirmed. The source IP in the initial alert (10.0.5.14) appears to be a misattribution; all evidence points to 10.0.5.42 as the true compromised host.
